- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak or use 2-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show price moving away from 65–70 range, model tends to overreact; apply 1–2% downward correction if sentiment is neutral or negative.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates late-period (last 7–10 days) price increases; adjust forecast by +1–2% for final 7 days if sentiment is positive.
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.00, 0.67), model may misread momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days to anchor forecast.
